limits: Automatic geometry LOD changes distant silhouettes and interpolation; it is not pixel-identical to full detail. No plants, root attributes, anchors, mean-water planes, authored placement or full-detail indices changed. The exact-array oracle covers 14 kinds and authored dry/sea records.

All 14 kinds with three roots each: 2250 to 1422 indices (36.8 percent). Authored eligible meadow meshes: 12477 to 9711; sea sample: 120030 to 79668. Additional far index storage is 4 bytes per far index; vertices are shared.

Wide meadow visible/shadow primitives: 136073/129315 to 135273/127983. Near/middle/wide full-detail restorations are exact on all three backends. Pressure uses lod_bias 4 and preserves captured pixels at all three views; it deliberately saves little geometry there.

The 800x600 kelp view is exact near, differs at 39 middle and 2004 wide pixels, peak 5/24 respectively. The far shoreline boundary and per-vertex mean-depth approximation remain subject to the pre-existing underwater limits.

Conservative culling suppresses only fully faded roots: 36 m plants and 32 m mounds, with a 10 cm hide margin. At most 50 cm travel can be skipped, tightened by distance from any hidden bound to its live fade with a 5 cm safety margin. New installs use the latest material focus and invalidate the cached scan.

Culling saves 2 to 15 visible draws in three local ground-focus samples. Teleporting away saves 142 (RD) or 160 (Compatibility) visible draws from the retained fixture; normal streaming separately removes distant chunks. Do not present teleport figures as steady-state speedups.

Cached bounds and travel allowance reduce the immediate-loop mean to about 8.7 us across 240 updates / 80 chunks (48 actual scans), with a 0 us stationary median at timer resolution. Rendered-loop means are roughly 17-23 us in the recorded samples. These are scoped costs, not complete-frame savings.
Viewport timing order is noisy/mixed and other Godot processes were present. No net FPS, battery, Android or browser claim. The desktop Mobile backend uses an RTX 3090, not mobile hardware.

The mound mesh keeps its existing dense topology. Four culling comparisons and the original deformation, exposed-trough and restoration checks pass on Forward+. Earlier Mobile mound restoration and shared-wind/mean-depth limits remain open.

Shader density thinning still submits intermediate-range plants. GPU survivor compaction, remaining regional sets, desktop/device route acceptance and all other renderer/gameplay roadmap work remain open. U45 is still the first gameplay issue after renderer work.
